# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Senek_2018_levodopa_carbidopa"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Senek_2018_levodopa_carbidopa"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s00228-018-2497-2> (open access, CC BY 4.0)

Levodopa/carbidopa 5/1.25 mg microtablets (Flexilev) are dispensed by an
automatic dose dispenser so that a Parkinson's disease patient can take small,
individually timed doses. Senek 2018 pooled two single-dose studies, one in
healthy volunteers and one in patients with motor fluctuations, and fitted one
joint population PK model for levodopa (LD) and carbidopa (CD). Both analytes
show double-peak profiles, which the model reproduces with two parallel
transit-compartment absorption chains per analyte: a fraction `fa1` of the dose
passes through a fast chain and the rest through a slow one.

Carbidopa inhibits peripheral dopa decarboxylase, and in the model the total
carbidopa dose lowers levodopa CL/F hyperbolically: 15% lower at 75 mg than at
50 mg of carbidopa. Levodopa CL/F also falls with Hoehn and Yahr stage (18%
from stage 1 to 4), and carbidopa CL/F falls with age (28% from 60 to 80
years).

# Population

The model-development data are 36 subjects from two single-centre, open-label,
single-dose microtablet studies (Senek 2018 Table 1):

* **Study 1**: 18 healthy volunteers (9 M / 9 F), age 26.0 +/- 6.2 years
  (19-46), body weight 71.7 +/- 11.3 kg (59-95). Single dose of 100/25 mg
  LD/CD, i.e. 20 microtablets dispersed in 100 mL water, sampled to 24 h.
* **Study 2**: 18 patients with Parkinson's disease and motor fluctuations
  (13 M / 5 F; one of 19 enrolled patients was excluded for an extreme
  triple-peak profile), age 71.4 +/- 6.3 years (61-82), body weight
  75.4 +/- 11.0 kg (55-96), Hoehn and Yahr stage 3.2 +/- 0.9 (2-5), 9.6 years
  since diagnosis. After an overnight washout they took 150% of their
  individual levodopa-equivalent morning dose, 110/27.5 to 410/102.5 mg
  (mean 275/68.75 mg), and were sampled to 6 h.

**Study 3** (10 healthy volunteers, 4 M / 6 F, age 24.7 +/- 4.3 years, body
weight 71.3 +/- 13.7 kg) received 75/18.75 mg followed by five doses of
45/11.25 mg every 2.4 h. It was used only for the external evaluation of the
levodopa model (Fig. 2), not for fitting.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Senek_2018_levodopa_carbidopa")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment in
`inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Senek_2018_levodopa_carbidopa.R`; the table
collects them. Table 2 values are the NONMEM point estimates (first two value
columns), not the SIR medians.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| LD two-compartment, CD one-compartment disposition | -- | Results, 'Base model' |
| Two parallel transit chains per analyte; dose split `fa1` / `1 - fa1` | -- | Methods, 'Base model'; Results, 'Base model' |
| Transit compartments: LD 5 (fast) and 6 (slow), CD 3 and 10 | -- | Results, 'Base model' |
| Allometric `P = TVP * (WT/70)^E`, E = 0.75 for CL/F and Q/F, 1 for VC/F and VP/F | -- | Methods, 'Covariate model', first display equation |
| Linear covariate `P = TVP * (1 + coeff * (COV - mean))` | -- | Methods, 'Covariate model', second display equation |
| Carbidopa-dose interaction `CL/F = TVCL / (1 + CDAMT / INTER)` | -- | Methods, 'Covariate model', third display equation |
| Covariate means: sex 0.389, age 48.7 y, HY 1.53 | -- | Table 1 footnote |
| Pre-dose concentration decaying at the terminal slope | -- | Methods, 'Base model' |
| `lcl` (LD CL/F, 0 mg CD, HY 1.53) | `log(1.31)` L/min | Table 2 and footnote dagger |
| `lvc`, `lq`, `lvp` | `log(45.4)` L, `log(0.667)` L/min, `log(44.9)` L | Table 2 |
| `lmtt1`, `lmtt2` (LD) | `log(16.1)`, `log(86.2)` min | Table 2 |
| `logitffo` (LD `fa1`) | `logit(0.749)` | Table 2 (logit scale, footnote double-dagger) |
| `lfdepot` (LD Frel) | `fixed(log(1))` | Table 2 '1 FIX' |
| `lc0` (LD pre-dose) | `log(0.120)` ug/mL | Table 2 |
| `led50` (INTER) | `log(86.7)` mg | Table 2 'INTERCL/F-CDAMT' |
| `e_dis_pd_hy_cl` | `fixed(-0.0616)` | Table 2 'CL/F-HY' |
| `e_age_fdepot` | `fixed(0.00172)` | Table 2 'FREL-AGE' |
| `lcl_carbidopa`, `lvc_carbidopa` | `log(1.05)` L/min, `log(168)` L | Table 2 |
| `lmtt1_carbidopa`, `lmtt2_carbidopa` | `log(34.6)`, `log(121)` min | Table 2 |
| `logitffo_carbidopa` (CD `fa1`) | `logit(0.570)` | Table 2 |
| `lfdepot_carbidopa` | `fixed(log(1))` | Table 2 '1 FIX' |
| `lc0_carbidopa` | `log(0.0256)` ug/mL | Table 2 |
| `e_age_cl_carbidopa`, `e_dis_pd_hy_cl_carbidopa`, `e_sexf_mtt2_carbidopa` | `fixed(-0.0119)`, `fixed(0.0141)`, `fixed(0.178)` | Table 2 'CL/F-AGE', 'CL/F-HY', 'MTT2-SEX' |
| `e_wt_*` allometric exponents | `fixed(0.75)` / `fixed(1)` | Methods, 'Covariate model' |
| IIV variances | `(CV/100)^2` | Table 2 'IIV' rows (see Assumptions) |
| Residual SDs, healthy / patients | LD 0.150 / 0.0702 and 0.00406 / 0; CD 0.0770 / 0.0386 and 0.00415 / 0.00684 | Table 2 'Proportional error', 'Additive error'; Results ('fixed to 0') |

# Reproducing the paper's derived numbers

The Results and Discussion quote several typical-value consequences of the
covariate model. These are closed-form functions of the `ini()` values, so the
check is exact: it confirms the functional forms, the covariate centring and
the sex coding in one pass.

```{r derived}
p <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Senek_2018_levodopa_carbidopa"))$theta

cl_ld <- function(cd_mg, hy, wt = 70) {
  exp(p[["lcl"]]) * (wt / 70)^0.75 * (1 + p[["e_dis_pd_hy_cl"]] * (hy - 1.53)) *
    exp(p[["led50"]]) / (exp(p[["led50"]]) + cd_mg)
}
cl_cd <- function(age, hy = 1.53, wt = 70) {
  exp(p[["lcl_carbidopa"]]) * (wt / 70)^0.75 *
    (1 + p[["e_age_cl_carbidopa"]] * (age - 48.7)) *
    (1 + p[["e_dis_pd_hy_cl_carbidopa"]] * (hy - 1.53))
}
vc_cd <- function(wt = 70) exp(p[["lvc_carbidopa"]]) * wt / 70
mtt2_cd <- function(sexf) {
  exp(p[["lmtt2_carbidopa"]]) * (1 + p[["e_sexf_mtt2_carbidopa"]] * (sexf - 0.389))
}
frel_ld <- function(age) 1 + p[["e_age_fdepot"]] * (age - 48.7)

derived <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~paper, ~model,
  "LD CL/F, 95 mg CD, HY 3, 70 kg (L/h)", 34, 60 * cl_ld(95, 3),
  "LD CL/F reduction, 75 vs 50 mg CD (%)", 15, 100 * (1 - cl_ld(75, 1.53) / cl_ld(50, 1.53)),
  "LD CL/F reduction, HY 1 to 4 (%)", 18, 100 * (1 - cl_ld(0, 4) / cl_ld(0, 1)),
  "LD total volume VC/F + VP/F (L)", 90, exp(p[["lvc"]]) + exp(p[["lvp"]]),
  "CD CL/F, 70 kg, 48.7 y (L/h)", 63, 60 * cl_cd(48.7),
  "CD VC/F, 70 kg (L)", 168, vc_cd(),
  "CD half-life, 70 kg, 48.7 y (min)", 111, log(2) * vc_cd() / cl_cd(48.7),
  "CD half-life, 75.4 kg, 71.4 y (min)", 155, log(2) * vc_cd(75.4) / cl_cd(71.4, wt = 75.4),
  "CD CL/F reduction, age 60 to 80 (%)", 28, 100 * (1 - cl_cd(80) / cl_cd(60)),
  "CD MTT2, women minus men (min)", 22, mtt2_cd(1) - mtt2_cd(0),
  "CD MTT2, women vs men (%)", 19, 100 * (mtt2_cd(1) / mtt2_cd(0) - 1),
  "LD Frel change, age 60 to 80 (%)", 3.4, 100 * (frel_ld(80) / frel_ld(60) - 1)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - paper) / paper)

knitr::kable(
  derived |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Derived quantity" = quantity,
      "Paper" = paper,
      "Model" = model,
      "% diff" = pct_diff
    ),
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Typical-value quantities quoted in Senek 2018 Results and Discussion, recomputed from the model parameters."
)

# Every quoted number is printed to 2 significant figures, so agreement within
# the rounding of the quote (< 3.5%) is the test.
stopifnot(all(abs(derived$pct_diff) < 3.5))
```

The carbidopa half-life at the patients' mean age (155 min) matches only with
the patients' mean body weight (75.4 kg) as well; at 70 kg it would be
152 min. Two further numbers in the paper do not reproduce and are discussed
under Assumptions and deviations.

# Virtual cohorts

Each simulated cohort has 100 subjects, with covariates drawn to match
Table 1. A dose is given into both dosing compartments of each analyte: the
model's `f()` assigns the fraction `fa1` to `depot` (fast chain) and `1 - fa1`
to `depot2` (slow chain), so each analyte needs two dose records of the full
amount.

```{r cohorts}
set.seed(2018)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2018)
n_sub <- 100

rtrunc_norm <- function(n, mean, sd, lo, hi) {
  pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean, sd), lo), hi)
}

cohort_study1 <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_sub),
  study = "Study 1 (healthy)",
  WT = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 71.7, 11.3, 59, 95),
  AGE = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 26.0, 6.2, 19, 46),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 9 / 18),
  DIS_PD_HY = 0,
  DIS_HEALTHY = 1,
  dose_ld = 100
)

# Study 2 doses are 150% of the individual morning dose in 5 mg microtablet
# steps (Table 1: 275 +/- 86.3 mg, range 110-410 mg). Hoehn and Yahr stage is
# drawn from {2, 3, 4, 5} with probabilities giving mean 3.2 and SD 0.98.
cohort_study2 <- tibble::tibble(
  id = n_sub + seq_len(n_sub),
  study = "Study 2 (patients)",
  WT = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 75.4, 11.0, 55, 96),
  AGE = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 71.4, 6.3, 61, 82),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 5 / 18),
  DIS_PD_HY = sample(2:5, n_sub, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1)),
  DIS_HEALTHY = 0,
  dose_ld = 5 * round(rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 275, 86.3, 110, 410) / 5)
)

cohort_single <- bind_rows(cohort_study1, cohort_study2) |>
  mutate(
    dose_cd = dose_ld / 4,
    # Single dose: the total carbidopa dose of the study is the dose itself.
    DOSE_CARBIDOPA_MG = dose_cd
  )

make_events <- function(cohort, dose_times, dose_ld_fun, obs_times) {
  doses <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(dose_index = seq_along(dose_times)) |>
    mutate(time = dose_times[dose_index], ld = dose_ld_fun(dose_index, dose_ld)) |>
    tidyr::crossing(cmt = c("depot", "depot2", "depot_carbidopa", "depot2_carbidopa")) |>
    mutate(
      amt = ifelse(grepl("carbidopa", cmt), ld / 4, ld),
      evid = 1L,
      dvid = NA_integer_
    ) |>
    select(-dose_index, -ld)
  obs <- cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(cmt = "central", amt = 0, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
    select(id, time, amt, cmt, evid, dvid, everything())
}

events_single <- make_events(
  cohort_single,
  dose_times = 0,
  dose_ld_fun = function(i, dose) dose,
  obs_times = c(0, 5, seq(10, 120, by = 10), seq(140, 360, by = 20), seq(420, 720, by = 60))
) |>
  filter(!(study == "Study 2 (patients)" & time > 360))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Senek_2018_levodopa_carbidopa")

sim_single <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_single,
  keep = c("study", "dose_ld", "dose_cd"),
  returnType = "data.frame",
  useLinCmt = FALSE
)
```

## Replicate Figure 1

Figure 1 of Senek 2018 is a prediction-corrected VPC of the observed data in
each study and analyte. The figure below shows the simulated individual
predictions (including between-subject variability, without residual error)
as the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles per nominal time. It is not
prediction-corrected, so the Study 2 band also carries the spread of the
individual doses.

```{r figure1, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6}
sim_long <- sim_single |>
  select(id, time, study, Cc, Cc_carbidopa) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cc_carbidopa), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "Cc", "Levodopa", "Carbidopa"))

vpc_single <- sim_long |>
  group_by(study, analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(conc, 0.10),
    p50 = quantile(conc, 0.50),
    p90 = quantile(conc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_single, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ analyte + study, scales = "free") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)",
    y = "Plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Senek 2018: median and 10th-90th percentile of simulated concentrations."
  )
```

The simulated medians peak near 0.75 ug/mL (levodopa) and 0.06 ug/mL
(carbidopa) in healthy volunteers and near 3 ug/mL and 0.24 ug/mL in
patients, close to the observed medians of Fig. 1. In the patient panels the
curves start from the pre-dose concentration left over from previous
treatment.

## Replicate Figure 2 (external evaluation, Study 3)

Study 3 gave 75/18.75 mg and then 45/11.25 mg every 2.4 h (144 min), six doses
in all. As in the paper, the levodopa CL/F of every Study 3 subject uses the
TOTAL carbidopa dose of the regimen, 18.75 + 5 x 11.25 = 75 mg.

```{r study3}
cohort_study3 <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 2 * n_sub + seq_len(n_sub),
  study = "Study 3 (healthy, multiple dose)",
  WT = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 71.3, 13.7, 52, 100),
  AGE = rtrunc_norm(n_sub, 24.7, 4.3, 20, 32),
  SEXF = rbinom(n_sub, 1, 6 / 10),
  DIS_PD_HY = 0,
  DIS_HEALTHY = 1,
  dose_ld = 45,
  DOSE_CARBIDOPA_MG = 18.75 + 5 * 11.25
)
stopifnot(all(cohort_study3$DOSE_CARBIDOPA_MG == 75))

dose_times_3 <- 144 * (0:5)
events_study3 <- make_events(
  cohort_study3,
  dose_times = dose_times_3,
  dose_ld_fun = function(i, dose) ifelse(i == 1, 75, dose),
  obs_times = sort(unique(c(seq(0, 860, by = 10), dose_times_3 + 20, dose_times_3 + 40)))
)

# The six doses deliver 300 mg levodopa and 75 mg carbidopa per subject.
dose_check <- events_study3 |>
  filter(evid == 1, id == min(id)) |>
  group_by(analyte = grepl("carbidopa", cmt)) |>
  summarise(total = sum(amt) / 2)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(sort(dose_check$total), c(75, 300))))

sim_study3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events_study3,
  keep = "study",
  returnType = "data.frame",
  useLinCmt = FALSE
)
```

```{r figure2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
vpc_study3 <- sim_study3 |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p10 = quantile(Cc, 0.10),
    p50 = quantile(Cc, 0.50),
    p90 = quantile(Cc, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_study3, aes(time, p50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)",
    y = "Levodopa plasma concentration (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Senek 2018 (Study 3): median and 10th-90th percentile."
  )
```

The observed medians in Fig. 2 rise to about 0.6-0.8 ug/mL after each dose and
fall to about 0.2 ug/mL before the next. The paper reports that the model
over-predicts the first-dose concentrations, which it attributes to the total
carbidopa dose being applied from time zero rather than accumulating.

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the simulated single-dose profiles, per study
and analyte. The PKNCA dose is the dose of the analyte (one of each pair of
dose records, since both carry the full amount).

```{r pknca}
conc_nca <- sim_long |>
  filter(!is.na(conc)) |>
  rename(treatment = study) |>
  select(id, time, conc, treatment, analyte)

dose_nca <- cohort_single |>
  select(id, treatment = study, Levodopa = dose_ld, Carbidopa = dose_cd) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Levodopa, Carbidopa), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "amt") |>
  mutate(time = 0)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_nca, conc ~ time | treatment + analyte + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | treatment + analyte + id)

intervals <- data.frame(
  treatment = c("Study 1 (healthy)", "Study 2 (patients)"),
  start = 0,
  end = c(720, 360),
  cmax = TRUE,
  tmax = TRUE,
  auclast = TRUE,
  half.life = TRUE
)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "auclast", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, analyte, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

knitr::kable(
  nca_summary |>
    dplyr::rename(
      "Study" = treatment,
      "Analyte" = analyte,
      "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
      "Tmax (min)" = tmax,
      "AUC0-last (ug*min/mL)" = auclast,
      "t1/2 (min)" = half.life
    ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Median simulated NCA parameters per study and analyte."
)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

Senek 2018 itself reports no NCA table. Its Discussion compares the model's
carbidopa half-life in the patients with the non-compartmental estimate from
the original Study 2 publication (Senek 2017), 171 +/- 37 min, and notes that
the model value (155 min) is "somewhat lower". The simulated cohort shows the
same shortfall; its median is a little lower again because the simulated
patients' Hoehn and Yahr stages (mean 3.2) raise carbidopa CL/F by about 2%
over the reference stage of 1.53 used for the 155 min.

```{r nca-compare}
cd_patients <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(treatment == "Study 2 (patients)", analyte == "Carbidopa", PPTESTCD == "half.life")
stopifnot(nrow(cd_patients) == n_sub)

simulated_nca <- cd_patients |>
  transmute(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~PPTESTCD, ~PPORRES,
  # Senek 2018 Discussion, citing the NCA of Senek 2017 (reference 6): mean
  # carbidopa half-life 171 +/- 37 min in the Study 2 patients.
  "Study 2 (patients)", "half.life", 171
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = simulated_nca,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "min"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp |>
    dplyr::rename("Study" = treatment),
  caption = "Carbidopa half-life in Parkinson's disease patients: median of the simulated cohort vs the published NCA mean."
)

# The paper's own model value (155 min) is 9% below the NCA and the simulated
# median about 13% below. Dropping the age effect would put it near 113 min
# (-34%), and a volume or clearance mis-transcription moves it further, so a
# 25% band separates those errors from cohort-sampling noise (about 3% SE on a
# median of 100 subjects).
stopifnot(abs(median(cd_patients$PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE) - 171) / 171 < 0.25)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **IIV scale.** Table 2 prints IIV as "CV%". It is read as `100 * sqrt(omega^2)`
  (variance = (CV/100)^2) rather than the log-normal `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`,
  for two reasons: the table footnote reports the RSEs "on the approximate
  standard deviation scale", which is the PsN `sumo` convention of reporting
  `sqrt(omega^2)`; and the unfixed-coefficient column prints the levodopa
  pre-dose IIV as `1.80` where the main column prints `180`. The two readings
  agree for the small omegas but not for the pre-dose concentrations: under
  the log-normal reading the levodopa pre-dose variance would be
  `log(1 + 1.8^2) = 1.44` instead of 3.24.
* **Distribution of the absorption IIV.** Methods says IIV was "log-normal or
  normal (absorption-related parameters)". `fa1` is explicitly normal on the
  logit scale and is encoded that way. MTT1, MTT2 and Frel are encoded
  log-normal: a normal (`TV * (1 + eta)`) IIV of 48% on the carbidopa Frel would
  give negative bioavailabilities in about 2% of subjects, which NONMEM would
  reject.
* **Transit rate constant.** `ktr = (n + 1) / MTT`, with `n` transit compartments
  between the dosing compartment and the central compartment, following
  Savic 2007, the paper's reference for the transit model. The paper does not
  print the formula.
* **Pre-dose concentration.** Applied to patients only (`DIS_HEALTHY = 0`). The
  Methods introduce it for the residual levodopa and carbidopa that Study 2
  patients carried over despite overnight washout, and the Study 1 and Study 3
  panels of Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 start at zero. It is placed at the time of the
  dose as an initial amount in the central compartment (and, for levodopa, the
  matching peripheral amount on the slow eigenvector), so that it decays
  mono-exponentially at the individual terminal slope, as the paper describes.
  The paper's observed pre-dose samples were taken up to 1 h before dosing.
* **Shared residual error not encoded.** The paper estimates that 28.5% of the
  total residual error is shared between levodopa and carbidopa measured in the
  same sample. nlmixr2 has no construct for a residual correlation across
  endpoints, so each analyte's residual error is encoded independently. The
  marginal residual distribution of each analyte is unchanged; only the
  correlation between them is lost.
* **Residual error form.** The table gives proportional and additive terms per
  analyte and population with no further detail; they are combined as
  `Var = (prop * C)^2 + add^2`. The levodopa additive term in patients was
  "estimated to a low value ... and therefore fixed to 0".
* **Unfixed-coefficient variant not shipped.** Table 2 also reports a model
  with re-estimated covariate coefficients and the weaker relationships
  removed (INTER 119.1 mg, levodopa HY coefficient -0.0967, carbidopa age
  coefficient -0.0114, no Frel-age, no carbidopa HY, no sex on MTT2). The paper
  presents it as a sensitivity check of the fixed AALASSO coefficients, so only
  the final model is encoded.
* **Inconsistent levodopa CL/F example.** The Results state that INTER = 86.7 mg
  "results in a LD CL/F estimated to 48.5 L/h with 50 mg CD and 40 L/h with
  75 mg CD, for a 70-kg subject". The model gives 49.9 and 42.1 L/h (at the
  mean HY of 1.53). The quoted pair implies a 17.5% reduction, while the
  Abstract quotes 15% for the same comparison, which the model reproduces
  exactly. The Table 2 parameters and the Abstract are taken as authoritative.
* **Carbidopa HY effect.** The Results describe the carbidopa CL/F change from
  HY 1 to 4 as "a very modest and clinically insignificant increase of 0.4%".
  The coefficient 0.0141 gives 4.3% (`(1 + 0.0141 * 2.47) / (1 - 0.0141 * 0.53)`),
  and the same formula reproduces the levodopa HY statement (18%) exactly, so
  0.4% is taken to be a dropped digit.
* **Direction of the age effect on levodopa Frel.** The Results call it "a
  decrease of 3.4% between the age 60 to 80 years", the Discussion "slightly
  increased with age (3.4% ...)". The coefficient is positive (0.00172), so
  Frel increases with age; the model follows the coefficient.
* **Carbidopa dose covariate.** `DOSE_CARBIDOPA_MG` is the total carbidopa dose
  over the study period, as in the paper. For a multiple-dose regimen this
  applies the full inhibition from the first dose.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Table 1 gives means, SDs and ranges only; covariates are
  drawn from normal distributions truncated to the reported ranges, and the
  Study 2 Hoehn and Yahr distribution is an assumed discrete distribution with
  the reported mean.
